name: DotNetNuke (DNN) - Authenticated RCE (SQL Console + File-Extension Bypass)
description: DotNetNuke (DNN) is the '.NET WordPress' CMS. With SuperUser/admin credentials (often pillaged from a web.config on an open share), two built-in features give code execution: the SQL console under Settings can enable xp_cmdshell for direct OS commands, and the Allowable File Extensions list can be widened to permit .asp/.aspx so an ASPX webshell can be uploaded via the File Management page. The web/SQL service typically holds SeImpersonate, so PrintSpoofer/JuicyPotato escalates straight to SYSTEM.

variations.label: RCE path 2 - widen Allowable File Extensions, upload ASPX webshell
variations.command:
# Settings > Security > More > More Security Settings -> add asp,aspx to Allowable File Extensions -> Save
# then http://<ip>/admin/file-management -> upload webshell.asp -> right-click > Get URL -> browse to run commands

variations.label: Escalate to SYSTEM via SeImpersonate (files land in Portals\0)

examples.label: Fingerprint DNN + find the admin login
Credentials commonly pillaged from a DNN web.config on an open NFS/SMB share
Confirm command execution through the SQL console

notes: Two independent RCE routes once logged in as a DNN SuperUser: (1) the SQL console (Settings page) enables xp_cmdshell and runs OS commands directly - the MSSQL service context usually has SeImpersonate; (2) if the SQL console is locked down, extend Allowable File Extensions to include asp/aspx and upload an ASPX webshell through /admin/file-management, then 'Get URL' to execute. Uploaded files land in C:\DotNetNuke\Portals\0 - re-widen extensions to also allow .exe so you can drop PrintSpoofer64.exe + nc.exe and pivot SeImpersonate -> NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. From SYSTEM: reg save SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY -> secretsdump for local + cached domain creds. This is the DEV01 foothold in the M28 capstone; it reuses mssql-enable-xpcmdshell and seimpersonate-printspoofer but the DNN-specific admin/upload vectors are unique.

references.title: DNN - Allowable file types and extensions for upload

recommended.note: Enumerate/mount the open NFS share that leaks the DNN web.config credentials.
The xp_cmdshell enablement this card drives from the DNN SQL console.
Escalate the webshell/SQL context (SeImpersonate) to SYSTEM.

defense.prerequisites: Valid DNN SuperUser/administrator credentials (frequently recovered from a web.config left on an anonymously accessible NFS/SMB share). HTTP access to the DNN admin UI.
defense.why_it_works: DNN ships two admin features that are code-execution primitives by design: a SQL console that can toggle and call xp_cmdshell, and a configurable upload allow-list that can be widened to server-executable extensions (.asp/.aspx). Neither is a CVE - it is built-in functionality abused with admin rights.
defense.misconfiguration: web.config with cleartext admin password exposed on an open share; SuperUser access to the SQL console; upload allow-list editable to include executable extensions; MSSQL/app pool running with SeImpersonate.
defense.impact: Remote code execution on the DNN/IIS host as the service account, then SeImpersonate -> SYSTEM, local SAM + cached domain credentials, and a foothold into the AD domain.
defense.detection: MSSQL: sp_configure changes enabling xp_cmdshell; xp_cmdshell process spawns (sqlservr.exe -> cmd.exe). Web: uploads of .asp/.aspx to Portals\0 or /admin/file-management; changes to Allowable File Extensions; new admin logins from unusual IPs.
defense.artifacts: SQL Server error/audit log (xp_cmdshell enabled); IIS logs showing webshell requests; new .asp/.aspx/.exe files under C:\DotNetNuke\Portals\0; DNN event log admin-login and settings-change entries.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# DNN admin can run Settings > SQL console
# Allowable File Extensions editable to asp,aspx,exe
# web.config readable on an 'everyone' NFS export
defense.secure_config:
# Remove/secure web.config from all shares; no anonymous NFS/SMB exports
# Restrict DNN SuperUser; disable the SQL console for non-DBA roles
# Keep upload allow-list to non-executable types; run MSSQL app pool without SeImpersonate
# Enforce least privilege on the service account
defense.prevention: Never store cleartext creds in web.config on shares; lock down anonymous file shares. Restrict SuperUser accounts and disable/limit the SQL console. Keep the upload allow-list free of executable extensions. Remove SeImpersonate from service accounts where possible. [MITRE M1035, M1022, M1026, M1018]
defense.evasion: Rename the webshell to an innocuous name; delete PrintSpoofer/nc after obtaining SYSTEM; run xp_cmdshell sparingly to avoid noisy sqlservr->cmd spawns.
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): file saved using client-supplied name/extension; MIME trusted from the request.
  move_uploaded_file(..., $_FILES['f']['name'])  |  extension blacklist  |  type check on $_FILES['f']['type'] (client-controlled)
GREP:  grep -rniE "move_uploaded_file|\$_FILES|multer|formidable|MultipartFile|SaveAs\(" .
SAFE:  extension ALLOWLIST + magic-byte MIME (finfo/mime_content_type), server-generated random filename, store outside webroot in a no-execute dir.
